fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Clear dense vegetation along the driveway to maintain an unobstructed path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Trim any shrubs or tree branches that overhang or narrow the driveway approach.
• Post the address visibly at the detached structure if it sits away from the main residence.
• Mark or label gate access points so responders can quickly identify which entry leads to which part of the property.
• Keep all fence gates unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch to allow rapid responder entry.
• Clear a flat, open staging area near the main residence where responders can set up equipment without repositioning vehicles.
• Remove or relocate parked vehicles from areas that block turnaround space for emergency vehicles.
• Keep the turnaround area free of stored equipment, landscaping materials, or other items that reduce maneuvering room.
• Trim dense vegetation near the detached structure to keep a clear path between it and the main residence.
• Keep walkways to all entry points clear of obstructions so responders can move quickly on foot between structures.
• Cut back any landscaped plantings that block sightlines between the street, driveway, and front entry area.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the house on all sides where vegetation is close to the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster to create open space between individual trees and reduce the amount of connected vegetation leading toward the house.
• Keep grass areas near the house mowed short, especially during dry periods when grass dries out and carries fire easily.
• Remove or cut back scattered shrubs that sit between the tree cluster and the structures to reduce connected plant material across the property.
• Maintain open ground between the base of scattered trees and any nearby buildings by removing low-hanging branches and shrubs growing beneath the trees.
• Keep irrigated landscaping beds immediately next to the house free of dead plant material, dry mulch, and woody debris.
• Separate shrubs from one another where they grow in groups near structures so fire cannot move easily from plant to plant.
• Clear any grass, leaves, or loose plant debris that has collected against exterior walls, under decks, or near entryways.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
